chapter_title: Chương 265: 0267【Mồm mép Trần cãi chày bắn như điên】

segments.title: Chương 265: 0267【Mồm mép Trần cãi chày bắn như điên】
segments.content:
After the representatives from the major websites returned, they all began to modify their account registration interfaces.

For Hainei.com, it wasn't a big deal. The Youke Huyou Platform, the Three Kingdoms Kill registration interface, and so on, already had options to fill in information like name, ID card number, phone number, and email.

It was just that it hadn't been mandatory before. You could fill it in or not, and even filling it with nonsense was fine.

Now, it was simply a matter of adding an asterisk in front of some of the optional fields, turning them into required information. But there was still no way to verify it, so users could still fill in nonsense.

They also sent out internal site messages to users, requesting that already registered users complete their personal information by the end of the year.

If they didn't complete their personal registration information, they would be unable to log in after New Year's Day next year.

A chorus of curses erupted!

Of course, they weren't cursing the websites, but the relevant authorities.

Because it wasn't just one or two websites doing this, but many websites making changes at the same time, everyone understood that the order came from above.

Four months ago, when the draft for public comment was announced, netizens who saw the news had already started cursing.

The editors at Hainei.com were under immense pressure. Accounts that usually made out-of-line comments now swarmed to take the opportunity to write inflammatory articles.

If it were just cursing and incitement, it would still be within an acceptable range. After all, the internet was very lenient in this era.

But someone started a rumor slandering historical sages and martyrs!

Over a hundred Xiaonei.com accounts were added to the blacklist system. They could still continue to post, but they would receive warning notifications from the website, and articles with serious issues would be blocked.

When these people found their articles blocked, most chose to stay on Hainei.com because they had already accumulated a large number of followers.

But they also went to other websites to register accounts, and while spreading rumors slandering sages and martyrs, they cursed Chen Guiliang and Hainei.com as shameless running dogs.

It was at this time that Luo Taijun's Niubo.com went online.

Never mind the more strictly moderated Hainei.com, even the leniently moderated Sina Blog couldn't tolerate some of the so-called opinion leaders.

These opinion leaders flocked to Niubo.com, because there, you could say whatever you wanted.

Its founding slogan was: Never delete posts!

Don't give me that bullshit about how Luo Taijun would have been arrested long ago if he had broken the law.

From its launch to its shutdown, Niubo.com never obtained an ICP operating license, because its application failed to pass the review.

This blog website operated illegally from beginning to end.

To avoid being forcibly shut down, it set up a mirror server in the United States in 2007, and in 2009, it moved its servers to the US entirely.

Just as the major websites were busy implementing the real-name system, this year's China Internet Conference was held.

Chen Guiliang attended on behalf of ByteDance and Game Science.

Ao Yanchen and Guo Feng also attended the conference for ByteDance, while Qu Guohao and Dong Qianqiu attended for Game Science.

Many internet companies did this, sending several executives at once, because there were various sub-forums. Some discussed technology, some discussed operations, and some discussed strategy…

"Haha, my product was on *Xinwen Lianbo* too!"

Seeing Zhou Hongwei again, the guy started boasting the moment he opened his mouth.

Chen Guiliang asked curiously, "Which day's *Xinwen Lianbo*? Did you record it? I had someone record it the day they reported on the Three Kingdoms Kill league."

Pressed by Chen Guiliang, Zhou Hongwei could only smile awkwardly, "It was CCTV's *Wanjian Xinwen Lianbo*."

Chen Guiliang was speechless.

That thing is called *Wanjian Xinwen*. He really knew how to flatter himself.

It did rebroadcast the main content of *Xinwen Lianbo*, but it also added a lot of other news. Zhou Hongwei's product was probably in that added part.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What did CCTV News report about you?"

"360 Safe Guard, of course," Zhou Hongwei said. "The Ministry of Information Industry is cracking down on internet chaos this year. Besides your websites, they are also strictly regulating rogue software. My Qihoo Safe Guard is a sharp weapon for cleaning up rogue software, and CCTV, with its discerning eye, gave it a special report."

Chen Guiliang was speechless.

"Mr. Zhou, Mr. Chen, a pleasure to see you both!" A man from Shijiazhuang walked over.

Chen Guiliang shook his hand warmly, "Mr. Li, hello. I've long admired your name."

Li Xiang had also been in the spotlight these past two years. His Popo.cn (a graphics card site) had revenues of 20 million last year, and with the backing of venture capital, his net worth had already surpassed 100 million.

At the same time, he also founded Autohome, laying the foundation for his future venture, Li Auto.

At this moment, Chen Guiliang really wanted to ask Zhou Hongwei if he dared to say he specialized in fighting rogue software in front of Li Xiang.

The software download channel on Popo.cn also had the rogue practice of bundled installations, which was common in the industry at the time. Popo.cn was already quite conscientious, at least it didn't engage in malicious hijacking. Compared to Zhou Hongwei's previous 3721, it was nothing.

"Mr. Yang…" Li Xiang chatted with Chen Guiliang and Zhou Hongwei for a couple of sentences, then ran off to schmooze with others.

Zhou Hongwei also took off.

Chen Guiliang hadn't walked far when another young man came over to shake his hand, "Mr. Chen, hello, I'm Yu Chen from YeePay."

"Mr. Yu, a pleasure to meet you," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

The company YeePay was not very famous.

But as it developed, for every three airline tickets sold in China, one was processed through YeePay. Additionally, many in tourism, education, telecommunications, insurance, and even government services also chose to cooperate with YeePay.

Yu Chen said, "Youke's Ufubao is very similar to our YeePay. The technical architecture and payment model are very similar, but we're not competitors. You mainly focus on social networking and game payments, while our target clients are governments and enterprises. Is the technical lead for Ufubao here today? I'd like to have a chat with him."

"He's here. He'll also be at a sub-forum. I'll give you his number." Chen Guiliang took out his phone to give him Dong Qianqiu's number, and also exchanged numbers with Yu Chen.

Yu Chen was a co-founder of YeePay. Before returning to China, he had worked as a product manager at Oracle and had also joined Bell Labs.

In front of Chen Guiliang, he talked at length about the "Payment 2.0" model to catch up with the current "Web 2.0" trend.

After listening to his "Payment 2.0," Chen Guiliang wondered why it sounded so similar to Youke's Ufubao. Shouldn't all payment systems be designed that way?

But Yu Chen said that including YeePay and Ufubao, there were currently fewer than ten companies in China using the "Payment 2.0" model.

Chen Guiliang was greatly shocked. A product from a company under me is actually that impressive?

When he had asked Dong Qianqiu to create Ufubao, Chen Guiliang had only casually made a few suggestions. Some of those suggestions Dong Qianqiu couldn't even implement, yet unexpectedly, they were already at the forefront of the times.

Just then, a reporter from Sina.com came over, "Hello, gentlemen. After today's event, we'd like to do an exclusive interview with entrepreneurs for our 'Win in China Series.' You both qualify as contestants who have won in China. Would you have time for an interview?"

"I'm available," Yu Chen agreed first. He was in urgent need of raising his profile to promote his product.

Chen Guiliang also nodded, "I can do that."

Dozens of media outlets were present today, but among the online media, Sina was the officially designated partner.

After meeting a few more internet bosses, Chen Guiliang went to the conference hall and took his seat.

The morning was mainly the opening ceremony, with various leaders giving speeches and addresses. Listening for two or three hours made one drowsy, but you didn't dare to actually doze off.

Because within the deluge of platitudes, there were often one or two pieces of useful information.

The afternoon consisted of various forums, and there was even a dedicated international forum, with officials from the embassies of countries like the US, Japan, South Korea, the UK, and Denmark attending. The Hong Kong and Taiwan Internet Associations also sent representatives.

Chen Guiliang participated in the main forum and was scheduled to speak.

He was barely qualified enough for that now.

The first speaker at the main forum was the vice president of China Mobile.

The second was the economist Professor Zhang.

The third was Baidu's Li Yanhong.

Some of Li Yanhong's remarks made Chen Guiliang frown. This fellow actually publicly badmouthed Web 2.0, even saying it would trigger an internet bubble like the one back then.

To Chen Guiliang, these words were equivalent to someone saying the breakfast industry had no future when he himself was selling soy milk and fried dough sticks. If everyone started selling breakfast, it would cause the entire catering industry to collapse.

Was he crazy?

Just two months ago, you yourself launched Baidu Spaces, which also follows the Web 2.0 model. Yet you're saying this model has no future?

After about a dozen people had taken the stage, it was finally Chen Guiliang's turn to speak.

Qihoo's CEO, Qi Xiangdong, was actually scheduled before Chen Guiliang. Zhou Hongwei was the chairman, but Qi Xiangdong was the CEO. For major public speaking events, it was usually Qi Xiangdong who appeared.

This was because Qi Xiangdong was formerly a deputy bureau chief at Xinhua News Agency and was brought in by Zhou Hongyi to handle government and media relations.

Qi Xiangdong spoke at length about cracking down on rogue software and being committed to maintaining a clean and safe online environment, without mentioning a single word about his past as the general manager of 3721.

This made many people in the audience chuckle.

He really made the big shots of the internet world break into laughter.

The host said, "Alright, let's thank Mr. Qi for his wonderful speech. Maintaining the online environment is everyone's responsibility, and civilized internet use is also a part of building a harmonious society. Next, let's welcome Mr. Chen Guiliang, the founder of ByteDance and Game Science. Please welcome Mr. Chen!"

Chen Guiliang walked up to the podium. This was his first time speaking at the main forum.

He adjusted the microphone upward and said, "Just now, Mr. Li from Baidu said that he didn't sleep well last night because he had to give a speech today. I, on the other hand, slept very well. Young people need their sleep. It's the elderly who can't sleep."

"Hahaha!"

A burst of laughter erupted from below the stage.

Chen Guiliang was on stage as the founder of a top Chinese SNS website company, and Li Yanhong had just publicly disparaged the Web 2.0 model. It was as if Li Yanhong had just slapped him in the face.

At the same time, Li Yanhong's remarks had also displeased the founders of many new and rising internet companies.

Because a person of Li Yanhong's status speaking so carelessly in public would damage industry confidence. Especially since Li Yanhong had specifically mentioned that overheated venture capital would trigger an internet bubble. Would this affect venture capital firms?

It seemed like he was blowing a whistle, but in reality, he was smashing people's rice bowls!

The moment Chen Guiliang spoke his first sentence, they already guessed he was going to rebut someone.

The big shots sitting next to Li Yanhong subconsciously glanced at him, only to see the man's face was expressionless.

Chen Guiliang continued, "I would like to point out a few of Mr. Li's errors…"

"First, Mr. Li just said that the ratio of Chinese netizens to the total population is far behind even Vietnam's. This is a beautiful misunderstanding caused by statistics. China defines a netizen as a citizen aged 6 or above who uses the internet for at least 1 hour per week and has a stable connection. A large number of temporary users in internet cafes are not included in the statistics."

"And what about Vietnam? Anyone who has been online once a week is called a netizen. No time limit. It not only includes internet cafe users, but even students who go online in a computer lab with an internet connection are counted as netizens. How could the resulting number of netizens not be large?"

"Therefore, this statement by Mr. Li is debatable."

Li Yanhong's expression soured a little.

Chen Guiliang continued, "Mr. Li also just said that the market capitalization of China's largest listed internet company is only one-tenth of that of Japan's listed internet companies. It's one thing for Mr. Li to belittle his Chinese peers, but why belittle his own Baidu as well?"

"With Baidu's market cap, it should have no problem ranking in the top five among Japan's listed internet companies. Yet you say China's largest internet company by market cap is not even one-tenth of a Japanese company's? Have you done your research and statistics?"

"Coincidentally, I recently served as Professor Lin's research assistant. He asked me about the development of the internet, and I told him that in the future, there would only be two internet centers in the world: the United States and China. Afterward, I specifically looked up information on the internet in other countries. I feel that Japan's internet companies are doing quite poorly."

"I don't know why Mr. Li wants to boost others' morale while deflating our own!"

Li Yanhong's face had already turned dark.

The host reminded him, "Mr. Chen, the topic of your speech today is 'The Development of the Web 2.0 Model'."

"My apologies, the prelude was a bit long," Chen Guiliang said apologetically, then continued his rebuttal. "Mr. Li also said just now that there are problems with China's internet environment. You attack rogue software, you attack hacker activities, and you attack the free advertising model. I'd like to ask, why is it that when a user searches for Three Kingdoms Kill, the official Three Kingdoms Kill website ranks sixth in the search results? And the first few search results are advertisements! Is it a problem with the search engine's technology?"

The entire venue fell silent.

This string of verbal attacks was fierce and relentless.

The founders of the emerging internet companies, however, were all beaming with smiles. They felt that Chen Guiliang was their mouthpiece, and a much more awesome one at that.

Li Yanhong had been smashing their rice bowls just now, and they were all very unhappy. Now, someone was finally speaking up for them!

The leaders in attendance remained expressionless. Aside from those with vested interests, the others didn't care what conflicts arose among the internet bosses.

Besides, not only had Li Yanhong badmouthed Web 2.0, but he had also said that China's netizen ratio was lower than Vietnam's and that Chinese internet companies were inferior to Japanese ones. Where was that supposed to leave the supervising leaders' pride?

Fortunately, Chen Guiliang had stepped up to set the record straight, preventing the Chinese internet from being outdone by Japan and Vietnam.

Chen Guiliang was also saving the leaders' faces.

Chen Guiliang continued, "Mr. Li also said just now that the main income of Chinese internet companies comes from online games and mobile value-added services. He said that these two industries are not particularly large in the international internet industry. Before you said that, shouldn't you have checked with an international business consulting firm?"

"These two things are pillars of the internet industry worldwide. Their respective shares account for one-quarter to one-third of an internet company's revenue! A revenue share of one-quarter to one-third, and you call them small industries?"

"Is the online gaming industry, which the state vigorously supports, a small industry? Have you ever thought about why it's being supported?"

The host felt mentally exhausted. "Mr. Chen, please get to the topic of your speech."

Chen Guiliang said, "Alright. Mr. Li just said that Web 2.0 has no future. My topic next is the future development of Web 2.0. Although Mr. Li is pessimistic about Web 2.0, he did just launch Baidu Spaces, which shows he's still willing to try, even if he thinks the industry has no future…"

The host buried his face in his hands in pain.

The dozens of media reporters, on the other hand, were all inexplicably excited.

Li Yanhong suddenly stood up and left the venue. It was unclear whether he was going to the restroom or simply leaving early.

(The protagonist's rebuttals in this chapter are based on the actual content of Li Yanhong's speech at the Internet Conference that year. Aside from the points about Web 2.0's insufficient monetization methods and overheated investment being true, the rest of Li Yanhong's speech was complete nonsense.)
